lines.text: In 1859, America and Britain almost went to war over a pig.
lines.say: In eighteen fifty-nine, America and Britain almost went to war, over a pig.

lines.text: Both countries claimed the same small island, and nobody had settled who owned it.
Then an American farmer found a British pig eating his potatoes, and shot it.
He offered 10 dollars. The owner wanted 100.
lines.say: He offered ten dollars. The owner wanted a hundred.

lines.text: So America sent soldiers. And Britain sent warships.
Soon, 461 Americans with 14 cannons faced 5 warships carrying 2,140 men.
lines.say: Soon, four hundred and sixty-one Americans, with fourteen cannons, faced five warships, carrying two thousand, one hundred and forty men.

lines.text: Then a British admiral arrived, and refused to start a war over a pig.
Instead, the two armies shared the island, for 12 years.
lines.say: Instead, the two armies shared the island, for twelve years.

lines.text: They visited each other on holidays, and held sports days.
In 1872, the German emperor gave the island to America.
lines.say: In eighteen seventy-two, the German emperor gave the island to America.

lines.text: Nobody ever apologised to the pig.
